messages:
claire: starting change window for lm-service — rolling v2-quant-fallback to 8% globally, focusing asia-1. primary checks: p95, 5xx, regional routing and fallback behavior. deploy-bot: rollout started: lm-service -> v2-quant-fallback (8%). rollout id r-2026-07-01-05 :rocket:
pablo: watching SLO dashboards (/dash/slo/lm-service). I'll page if asia-1 p95 > 180ms or 5xx > 0.5%. :eyes:
nate: note: v2-quant-fallback adds a new regional fallback policy that should steer to cpu-quant variant on high tail latency. it's in the canary policy but not exercised yet.
telemetry-bot: perf smoke queued (30s). collecting p50/p95/p99, 5xx, and region-based routing metrics.
sre-bot: automated check: asia-1 p95 = 202ms in canary slice (baseline 135ms). alert id slo-4510. paging oncall in 2m.
pablo: ack. holding ramp. do not advance to 30%.
claire: did the fallback policy trigger? we expected automatic regional steer to cpu-quant when p95 > 170ms.
nate: looks like policy didn't engage — routing logs show fallback rule not matched due to missing tag on canary pods (tag: fallback-enabled=false). I pushed a quick label fix to the deployment template.
pablo: paste the query for routing mismatch?
nate: ```query
sum(rate(route_decisions_total{service=\"lm-service\",decision=~\"fallback|serve\"}[1m])) by (region,decision)
```
nate: results: asia-1 serve=12/s fallback=0/s (should be fallback=~8/s if policy applied)
claire: fix the labels and restart canary pods. we want to test regional fallback rather than full rollback.
nate: applying label fix:
```bash
kubectl label deployment/lm-service-canary fallback-enabled=true --overwrite -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/lm-service-canary -n prod
```
deploy-bot: rollout restart detected for lm-service-canary.
telemetry-bot: after restart: route_decisions in asia-1 show fallback=7.6/s, serve down to 6.1/s. canary asia-1 p95 trending to 150ms, 5xx down to 0.12%.
pablo: nice. so regional fallback to cpu-quant is working. suggestion: keep canary at 8% for 25m and observe. if asia-1 stabilizes we can resume ramp elsewhere. if other regions show similar tail regressions, we'll pin globally.
claire: agreed. note for release notes: tag the rollout with "fallback-exercised" and file follow-up to auto-validate fallback policies pre-rollout.
nate: filing INF-1200: "Validate fallback policy tags and simulate regional steer before ramp". link: https://issues.redwood/INF-1200
sre-bot: reminder: if we choose to pin use `deployctl pin --service lm-service --version v1-stable --reason \"canary p95 regression\"` (routes traffic back to v1 across regions).
pablo: adding that to the release notes. also add an operational play: verify routing logs for fallback decisions for 10m after any canary restart.
claire: thanks. keeping thread open. we'll reconvene in 25m to either continue ramp or pin. :thumbsup:
